newsitem.title: CONGO: S.Africa hopes for breakthrough in Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hopes for breakthrough in Zaire talks.

text.p: South African Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Wednesday he hoped for a breakthrough in imminent talks between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and his rebel rival, Laurent Kabila.
"There's no reason why we should not expect a breakthrough. That's why we're here," he told reporters aboard the South African navy icebreaker Outeniqua in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire.
Modise was among officials waiting for the arrival of Mobutu, Kabila and South African President Nelson Mandela.
"The fact that they are talking together will begin to put together the building blocks for a future stable state," he said.

Modise said no ceasefire had been agreed upon for the duration of the talks, in which Kabila was likely to repeat his insistence that Mobutu should resign immediately to avoid a rebel attack on the capital Kinshasa.

Officials left the ship earlier for a nearby airfield to meet Mandela, who will chair the second face-to-face encounter between Mobutu and Kabila. The two men held inconclusive talks aboard the same ship on May 4.

Modise was expected to fly to the nearby port of Soyo to collect Kabila and Mobutu, who suffers from prostate cancer, was expected to be driven aboard on a laoding ramp, as he was for the previous meeting.
The talks were initially scheduled to start at 11 a.m. (1000 gmt), but 10 minutes before that time there was no sign that they would begin on schedule.
